content.text:
# taskrun

A dependency-aware task runner with no dependencies of its own. It reads a task file from standard input and answers questions about it; it never executes a command.

## Layout

| File | What it owns |
| --- | --- |
| `src/cli.js` | the argument forms, the mode dispatch, and how a failure is reported |
| `src/parse.js` | the task-file grammar and the refusals it words, as `ParseError` |
| `src/graph.js` | run order over the dependency edges |
| `src/digest.js` | the FNV-1a digest the snapshot format records |

`test/taskrun.test.js` is the suite for what is already here. `data/files/` holds the workspace files the examples name, and `data/snapshots/` the digest snapshots.

## The task file

One directive per line. A line is trimmed first; an empty one and one that starts with `#` are ignored; the rest is split on runs of whitespace.

```
# build.tasks
task build node build.js
task bundle node bundle.js
needs bundle build
```

`task <name> <word>...` declares a task whose command is the remaining words joined with single spaces. `needs <name> <dependency>...` adds dependencies; a repeated edge counts once, and a `needs` line may stand before the `task` line it names.

## Modes

- `order` prints the task names one per line, in run order: repeatedly the lexicographically smallest task whose dependencies have all been printed.
- `show <name>` prints `<name>: <command>` and then `needs: ` followed by the dependencies in ascending order, or `-` when there are none.
- `digest <path>...` prints `<path> <digest>` for each path in argument order, with `missing` in place of a digest for a path that is not there. The digest is 32-bit FNV-1a over the file's bytes — offset basis `0x811c9dc5`, prime `16777619`, xor then multiply — as eight lowercase hex digits.

## Failures

Every refusal writes one line to standard error and exits 2, having written nothing to standard output; the first failure stops the run. A parse failure names its 1-based input line: `error: line 2: unknown directive run`. The messages are `expected task <name> <word>...`, `expected needs <name> <dependency>...`, `invalid task name <name>`, `task <name> is declared twice` and `unknown directive <word>`. A `needs` line naming a task no `task` line declares is refused without a line number, as `error: unknown task <name>`, and so is `show` on such a name.

## Known gaps

`order` does not detect a dependency cycle: it stops as soon as nothing is ready and leaves every task in the cycle out of its output. The task file has no way to declare which files a task reads or writes, so nothing here can tell whether a task is up to date.

  "prompt": "`taskrun` is the repository in this workspace: `README.md` describes what it already does, `src/` holds it, and `test/taskrun.test.js` is its own suite, which passes. Extend it so the task file can declare the files a task touches, so a dependency cycle is reported instead of silently truncating the order, and so a plan can say which tasks a snapshot leaves stale. Every behaviour `README.md` documents stays exactly as it is, including the wording and the exit code of every failure it lists, and the work spans the parser, the graph, and the command.\n\nTwo directives join the task file, parsed like the ones already there. `reads <name> <path>...` names input files of a task and `writes <name> <path>...` names its outputs; each takes at least one path, a repeated path counts once, and either line may stand before the `task` line it names, exactly as `needs` may. A path is one or more of the characters `A` to `Z`, `a` to `z`, `0` to `9`, `_`, `.`, `/` and `-`, does not begin with `/`, and holds no `..` segment; anything else fails with `error: line N: invalid path <path>`. A `reads` or `writes` line with fewer than two words after the directive fails with `error: line N: expected reads <name> <path>...` or `error: line N: expected writes <name> <path>...`. Every name a `reads` or `writes` line uses must be declared by a `task` line somewhere, on pain of the existing line-less `error: unknown task <name>`; as before, every failure that names a line is reported before that one, in line order.\n\n`files <name>` is a new mode taking exactly one name. It prints `reads: ` followed by that task's input paths in ascending order and then `writes: ` followed by its output paths in ascending order, each with `-` in place of an empty list, and it refuses an undeclared name the way `show` does. The usage line every malformed argument list reports becomes `error: usage: cli.js order|show <name>|files <name>|digest <path>...|plan <snapshot>`; `order` takes no further word, `show`, `files` and `plan` take exactly one, and `digest` takes at least one.\n\n`order` now refuses a cyclic graph: it writes `error: cycle: ` followed by the cycle's names joined with ` -> ` and ending with a repeat of the first name, then exits 3, having written nothing to standard output. The reported cycle is the first one a depth-first search finds when it starts from each task in ascending name order and walks each task's dependencies in ascending name order; it runs from the task the search re-entered, through the search stack, back to that task. A task that needs itself is such a cycle. `show`, `files` and `digest` never look at the graph, so they answer a cyclic file as they answer any other.\n\n`plan <snapshot>` reads a digest snapshot and reports what the graph would have to rerun. The snapshot file is a line per recorded path, trimmed, with an empty line and a line starting with `#` ignored, and the rest split on runs of whitespace into exactly two words: a path and its digest, which is exactly eight lowercase hexadecimal digits. A snapshot that cannot be read fails with `error: cannot read snapshot <path>`, and a malformed line fails with `error: <snapshot>: line N: ` followed by `expected <path> <digest>`, `invalid digest <word>`, or `path <path> is recorded twice`, where N counts the snapshot's own lines from 1. ## Summary

I extended `taskrun` to support file tracking, cycle detection, and incremental planning, touching only `src/`:

**`src/parse.js`** — added a `PATH` regex and `isPath` validator (allowed charset, no leading `/`, no `..` segment), and generalized the directive/attachment handling so `reads <name> <path>...` and `writes <name> <path>...` parse exactly like `needs` (forward references allowed, dedup on merge, arity and path-format errors raised immediately with line numbers, unknown-name errors raised afterward without one). Tasks now carry `reads` and `writes` arrays alongside `needs`.

**`src/graph.js`** — added `CycleError` and a `findCycle` DFS that visits tasks and their dependencies in ascending name order, using a recursion-stack to detect a re-entered active node and slice out the exact cycle path. `order()` now runs this check first and throws before falling back to the existing greedy topological sort, which (cycle-free) now always completes instead of silently truncating.

**`src/snapshot.js`** (new) — parses a digest snapshot's lines (trim, skip blanks/comments, require exactly `<path> <digest>` with an 8-digit lowercase-hex digest, reject duplicate paths), throwing a line-numbered `SnapshotError`.

**`src/cli.js`** — updated the usage string, added `files <name>` (prints sorted reads/writes with `-` for empty, reusing the `show`-style unknown-task check without touching the graph), and added `plan <snapshot>`: reads the task file, then the snapshot (in that order, so failures surface in the specified precedence), computes the run order (surfacing cycles as exit 3), then for each task in order checks its deduplicated, sorted watched paths for `new`/`missing`/`changed` reasons before falling back to the smallest already-run dependency (`needs <dep>`), emitting `run`/`skip` lines and the final `total run=<r> skip=<s>`.

No dependencies were added (`node_modules` absent) and nothing under `test/` or `package.json` was modified.
